Subject: Re: Altavista POC - initial discovery

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions before we sign the SOW. We want to validate two things for the pilot:

- Auth model: We'll use our API gateway (mTLS + JWT) in front of requests. Can Redwood accept inbound JWTs signed by our IdP, or do we need a token exchange?
- Quotas: We expect bursts (up to ~150 req/s) for short windows, steady-state ~20 req/s. What is the recommended quota guardrail vs. Dedicated capacity?

Also capture: structured outputs for tool calling (we have an internal tool router), and embeddings for reranking a 2M-doc index — latency will matter.

Attaching a short whiteboard and our rough traffic profile.

—Miguel
Senior Architect, Altavista AI

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Altavista POC - implementation questions & rate/quota follow-up

Miguel, Priya — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers and next steps below; copying Rishi for the runtime/SDK specifics.

1) Auth model: Redwood supports direct JWT acceptance if the JWT conforms to our accepted claims (iss, sub, exp) and is signed by a trusted IdP. If you prefer token exchange for short-lived Redwood API keys we can add a one-click exchange step in the POC runbook.

2) Quotas & bursts: For the pilot I recommend Dedicated burst policy + token-level quota. We can set a baseline quota at 30 req/s and allow bursts up to 200 req/s for 30s windows with backpressure rules. We'll include adaptive throttling to avoid cascades.

3) Embeddings + rerank: For 2M docs we recommend an embedding-only hotstore (SSD NVMe) with a specialized reranker endpoint. Expect 95th p99 query latency of ~120ms for a small top-k rerank if run on dedicated infra; we'll include a caching layer for repeated contexts.

4) Structured output/tool-calling: Redwood's structured output schema (JSON schema + function-call contract) maps to your tool router. Rishi will detail the SDK helper for calling tools from model responses and validating outputs.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi: send a short SDK snippet + recommended request-id pattern for idempotency and 429 handling.
- Marissa: we will schedule a follow-up to finalize SOW and quotas (can we target Tues 20th?).
- Miguel/Priya: confirm whether you want direct JWT acceptance or token exchange.

Attaching: altavista-poc-runbook-v1.pdf and token-flow.drawio.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Altavista POC - SDK snippets, retries & idempotency

Neha / Miguel — quick engineering follow-up with concrete patterns. Pasted examples are intentionally minimal so you can drop them into the POC.

--- SDK auth pattern (pseudo-JS) ---
// Accepts either incoming JWT (validated) or exchanged short-lived key
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, // exchanged token flow OR null if using JWT passthrough\  validateJwt: true,\});

// Request-id header pattern for idempotency
const requestId = `altavista-${Date.now()}-${Math.floor(Math.random()*1000)}`;

await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-retrieval-1',
  input: userPrompt,
  headers: { 'x-request-id': requestId },
});

--- Retries & 429 handling ---
Recommendations:
- Use exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 8s).
- Treat 429 and 503 as retryable; 4xx (other than 429) are not.
- Include x-request-id on retries so server can detect duplicates and return cached/consistent responses.
- Circuit-breaker at client level: after N consecutive 429s (N=5) pause attempts for 30s and call the Redwood /health endpoint.

--- Server-side behavior we will configure for the POC ---
- Token-level quotas (sliding window) + burst tokens for short windows.
- Automatic prefix caching for repeated contexts (reduces tokens billed + latency).
- Idempotency store: if x-request-id observed within idempotency window (60s) we return stored result. For longer windows we can wire a persistent idempotency cache (configurable).

I'll add a minimal retry helper and a small note on signature validation to the runbook (see attached retry-idempotency-patterns.md).

—Rishi
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks — that helps. Couple of clarifying items before the follow-up meeting:

- For idempotency: is the 60s idempotency window adjustable? We have some batched worker retries that could surface delayed duplicates. If adjustable, what's the operational cost?
- For embedding rerank: can you share the expected memory footprint numbers for the reranker node for 2M docs (embedding dim 1536)? We need to justify infra.
- Will the SDK helper surface structured output validation errors locally, or will those be surfaced only in Redwood console? We want early validation in our worker.

We can meet Tues 20th at 10am PT.

—Priya

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Altavista POC - implementation questions & rate/quota follow-up

Great questions, Priya — short answers and we'll cover in the call Tues 10am PT (calendar invite sent).

- Idempotency window: configurable. Default 60s (lightweight in-memory store). We can enable a persistent idempotency cache for the POC (configurable TTL up to 24h) — operational cost is modest (small Redis instance or our managed idempotency store). I'll include estimated monthly cost in the SOW addendum.
- Reranker footprint: approximate working set for 2M x 1536 float32 embeddings ~ 12.3 GB if using float32; with quantization to int8 it's ~3.2 GB + index overhead. We'll attach a short calc to the POC runbook.
- SDK validation: Rishi will add a local validation helper that validates structured output against a JSON schema before calling your router; console will still log full validation failures for visibility.

Action items:
- Rishi: add TTL options for idempotency cache and a small cost estimate to retry-idempotency-patterns.md.
- Marissa: finalize the POC SOW and include the persistent idempotency line item.
- Miguel/Priya: confirm JWT passthrough vs token exchange by EOD Mon.

Thanks — talk Tues.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
